Definition: from G2152; piety; specially, the gospel scheme:--godliness, holiness.
BiblicalUsage: eusébeia is the word for godliness, holiness. In Acts 3:12, the text says "as though by our own power or holiness we had made this man to walk?" In 1 Timothy 2:2, the text says "that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty."
TheologicalSignificance: eusébeia convinces me that faith is not a feeling but a holding-on — trusting what God has said when nothing else makes sense. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
